title: Campaign: retries and timeouts across the estate
_note: rv2 S2 (PLAN §2.2 campaign-<tag> row, tag retries-timeouts). Sources are 3 live campaign study quests from different repos per idea; recapAfter = any 3 sources passed. Server-local side file, never stamped.

ideas.idea: Retry only failures that can succeed later, with a capped, growing and jittered delay that the selection query itself respects.
ideas.why: A retry loop without backoff hammers a failing dependency within seconds, and retrying permanent errors only burns the attempt budget.
ideas.prompt: Failed refunds are picked up by a worker that selects every failed row on each tick. Within a minute a provider outage has used up all retry attempts. What is missing?
ideas.answer: A next-attempt time: each failure should schedule the row for later, growing the delay per attempt with a cap and some randomness, and the worker should only select rows whose time has come. Classify errors too: a declined card is permanent, a timeout is worth retrying.

ideas.idea: Give every outbound call and every running step a time budget, because a hung connection raises no error and no retry rule ever fires.
ideas.why: Without a deadline one slow vendor holds workers, connections and requests indefinitely, and the system looks busy rather than broken.
ideas.prompt: A workflow step waits on a vendor whose socket hangs without closing. Your retry policy handles errors well, yet runs stay 'running' for days. Why does the policy not help, and what do you add?
ideas.answer: A hang produces no error, so nothing triggers the retry. Put a timeout (an AbortSignal or client timeout) on the call and a duration budget on the step, then treat expiry as a retriable failure, so stuck runs are detected and retried or failed on purpose.

ideas.idea: A retried operation must carry an identity that stays the same across attempts, so the receiver can tell 'the same request again' from 'a new request'.
ideas.why: Without retry identity, every timeout followed by a retry risks doing the work twice: two orders, two charges, two usage events.
ideas.prompt: Checkout calls the payment API, times out, and retries. The customer is charged twice. The team proposes shorter timeouts. Why is that not the fix?
ideas.answer: A shorter timeout only changes when you give up; the first call may still succeed after you retry. Send a key that identifies this checkout attempt and keep it for every retry, so the provider performs the charge once and returns the same result to the second call.

ideas.idea: When a caller will retry on timeout (webhooks, queues), verify and record the request quickly, answer, and do the slow work afterwards from durable storage.
ideas.why: Doing all the work inline before replying makes the sender time out and resend, so the slow path runs again and again.
ideas.prompt: A payment webhook handler verifies the signature, then fulfils the whole order, emails included, before replying. The provider retries after 10 seconds and orders ship twice. Restructure it.
ideas.answer: Verify the signature, store the event by its id (ignoring ids already stored) and reply 2xx at once. A worker then fulfils the order from that stored event, with its own retries. The provider's retry now finds the event already recorded, and slow emails no longer hold the response.

ideas.idea: Log every attempt with the logical operation id, the attempt number, the outcome and the duration, so a retry storm or a stuck operation is visible.
ideas.why: Retries hide failures by design; without attempt-level logs an operation that failed five times and then succeeded looks healthy.
ideas.prompt: Usage events are replayed after an incident and some payments time out. Support asks which customers were affected and how many attempts each took. What should the logs already contain?
ideas.answer: One structured line per attempt: a trace id, a safe tenant identifier, the logical operation id, the attempt number, outcome and duration; never card data or secrets. Grouping by operation id then shows each customer's attempts, and counting attempts shows whether retries are rising.
